name: DRV8871 brushed DC motor driver
description: TI DRV8871 single H-bridge brushed DC motor driver with internal current sensing: runs one DC motor forwards, backwards, braked or coasting from two logic inputs (3.3 V or 5 V, PWM up to 200 kHz), motor supply 6.5-45 V, 3.6 A peak, current limit set by a resistor (30 kOhm fitted = about 2.1 A), sleeps when both inputs are low. Sold as: Adafruit DRV8871 DC Motor Driver Breakout Board - 3.6A Max (#3190), 4-pin header IN2 IN1 VM GND, plus a MOTOR screw terminal (OUT2, OUT1) and a POWER screw terminal (+ = VM, - = GND) on the opposite edge.
eli5: Lets your board make one DC motor spin forwards or backwards, using a separate battery or power supply for the motor.

pins.name: IN2
pins.description: Header pin 1: logic input 2, controls OUT2 (high >= 1.5 V, low <= 0.5 V, max 5.5 V; 100 kOhm pull-down; PWM for speed)

pins.name: IN1
pins.description: Header pin 2: logic input 1, controls OUT1 (high >= 1.5 V, max 5.5 V; 100 kOhm pull-down)

pins.name: VM
pins.description: Header pin 3: motor supply 6.5-45 V, also powers the chip (no logic supply needed). Same net as the POWER + terminal. Never connect to the microcontroller when an external supply is used

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Header pin 4: ground, shared by the motor supply (POWER - terminal) and the microcontroller

pins.name: OUT2
pins.description: MOTOR screw terminal (marked 2): motor output 2; connect the motor, never the microcontroller

supplierQuery: Adafruit DRV8871 DC motor driver breakout 3190
buildNotes: Truth table (TI datasheet Table 1): IN1 high/IN2 low = forward (OUT1 H, OUT2 L), IN1 low/IN2 high = reverse, both high = brake, both low = coast (outputs Hi-Z, then sleep after about 1 ms).
Motor supply 6.5-45 V into the POWER terminal or the VM pin (same net). Under-voltage lockout at about 6.1-6.4 V, so a 5 V USB supply will NOT run it.
Join the board GND to the microcontroller GND. Never connect VM to the microcontroller while an external supply is used.
Logic inputs take 0-5.5 V and count as high above 1.5 V, so 3.3 V GPIOs drive them directly. They have 100 kOhm pull-downs: unconnected inputs = coast/sleep.

Speed: PWM one input while holding the other high (drive/brake, slow decay; the motor drives while the PWM pin is low) or PWM one input with the other low (drive/coast). PWM up to 200 kHz; 20 kHz is silent.

Current limit ITRIP = 64 kV / RILIM (datasheet Eq. 1). The board's 30 kOhm gives about 2.1 A (1.97-2.3 A). Overcurrent above 3.7 A and overtemperature shut the bridge off and it retries after about 3 ms.
About 2 A RMS continuous on a typical board; 3.6 A only as short peaks.

example.code:
import time
from drv8871 import DRV8871

motor = DRV8871({IN1}, {IN2})
while True:
    motor.forward()
    print('motor forward')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor.coast()
    print('motor coasting')
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Runs the motor forward, then lets it coast

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (1 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
